claims.text: Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo in the as-cast condition is a disordered BCC solid solution.
As-cast equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo has a room-temperature compressive yield strength of approximately 1719 MPa.
As-cast equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo fails after only a few percent compressive strain at room temperature.
A 50% cold-work reduction followed by annealing at approximately 600°C for 30 minutes will refine the grain structure of equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo.
The proposed thermomechanical treatment will produce a more uniform distribution of smaller grains.
The proposed thermomechanical treatment will reduce internal residual stresses.
Grain refinement will decrease stress concentrations in the alloy.
Grain refinement will increase the density of grain boundaries.
The increased grain-boundary density will enhance dislocation mobility.
The refined microstructure will activate additional slip systems.
The disordered BCC matrix will retain its inherent solid-solution strengthening after processing.
The processed alloy will exceed 10% compressive strain at room temperature.
The processed alloy will retain compressive yield strength within approximately 10% of 1719 MPa.
The combined grain-boundary and solid-solution effects will improve plastic deformation while preserving high strength.
The strength-plasticity benefit requires processing that avoids full recrystallization and grain coarsening.
Excessive cold work or an anneal that is too hot or too long could negate the proposed strength and plasticity benefits.
